title: Analysis of Income Taxes
overview: Income-tax analysis explains temporary differences, deferred tax balances, effective rates, and realizability.
example: Follow one transaction through the income statement, balance sheet, cash-flow statement, and the resulting ratios.

modules.title: Differences Between Accounting Profit and Taxable Income
modules.explanation: Accounting income and taxable income differ because recognition rules and timing differ. Temporary differences create deferred tax assets or liabilities; permanent differences affect the effective tax rate without reversing later.
steps: Reconcile statutory tax with reported tax expense.
Classify each difference as temporary or permanent and determine its direction.
Assess reversal, realizability, valuation allowances, and sustainable cash tax rates.
modules.check: Explain how differences between accounting profit and taxable income changes an analyst's conclusion, including one limitation.
objectives: Explain differences between accounting profit and taxable income in plain language and connect it to the reading's central problem.
Apply the analytical decision rule or analytical decision rule with clearly labeled inputs.
Interpret the result, challenge its assumptions, and identify one condition that would change the conclusion.
lesson: Accounting income and taxable income differ because recognition rules and timing differ. Temporary differences create deferred tax assets or liabilities; permanent differences affect the effective tax rate without reversing later.

Statement analysis follows an economic event through recognition, measurement, presentation, disclosure, and cash flow. Comparability often requires adjustments because firms can represent similar economics with different estimates or classifications.
